title: Launch Sprint Debrief & Contingency Logbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a combined sprint debrief, KPI tracker snapshot, and operational contingency log for the upcoming hosted API + Dedicated capacity launch window. Built as a lightweight single-pane artifact for the cross-functional launch team to take quick decisions and execute runbook steps if signals deviate.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: internal launch of the new staged rollout for model routing + autoscaling for Dedicated (phase 1). Tracks high-level milestones, primary KPIs, known risks, and exact contingency actions.
- Audience: product-ops, eng-serving-runtime, SRE, GTM launch leads, solutions engineering on-call.

Quick snapshot (as of 2026-02-18):
- Launch window: 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-15 (phased ramp)
- Primary owners: Maya Patel (product-ops), Jordan Lee (SRE lead), Camila Ruiz (serving runtime PM)
- Canary cohort: 5 pilot customers (list owned in Confluence env page)
- Go/no-go top-line: Ready -> minor open infra action (autoscale fuzz)

Roadmap tracker (milestones, owner, ETA, status):
- Canary deploy to region us-west-2 | Owner: Camila Ruiz | ETA: 2026-03-01 | Status: planned
- Autoscaler policy tune v1 | Owner: Jordan Lee | ETA: 2026-02-25 | Status: in_progress (PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ramp-pr/342)
- Observability retention + dashboard refresh | Owner: Ben Thornton | ETA: 2026-02-26 | Status: in_review
- Customer success playbook + alerts | Owner: Maya Patel | ETA: 2026-02-28 | Status: draft

KPI sheet (baseline, target, early-warning thresholds):
- API p50 latency (text gen, 32 tokens): Baseline 85ms | Target <= 100ms | Warning: > 120ms sustained 5m
- API p95 latency (text gen): Baseline 240ms | Target <= 300ms | Warning: > 450ms for 3 consecutive minutes
- Tail error rate (5xx + timeouts): Baseline 0.3% | Target <= 0.5% | Critical: >= 1.0% 1m
- Average cost per 1k tokens (hosted path): Baseline $0.90 | Target <= $1.10 | Warning: +30% vs baseline 1h
- New customers onboarding success (first call OK): Baseline 92% | Target >= 95% | Warning: < 90% daily
- Model quality regression (evaluations on regression-suite): Baseline 0% regressions | Target 0 allowed | Warning: any regression on golden prompts

Monitoring & alert routing (who wakes up):
- Latency p95 breach -> Pager to eng-sre (on-call) and @product-ops (Jordan + Maya).
- Error spike (>=1% 1m) -> Immediate paging, follow rollback checklist.
- Cost surge (billing anomaly rule) -> Notify finance + product-ops, but do not auto-scale down without owner approval.
- Quality regression -> Alert to applied-ml + product, block rollout if regression confirmed.

Acceptable degradation profile for phased ramp:
- Phase 1 (0-10% traffic): p95 latency up to +20% over baseline tolerated; error rate must remain < 0.8%
- Phase 2 (10-50%): p95 latency +30% tolerated during warm-up windows; error rate must remain < 0.6%
- Phase 3 (50-100%): must meet target KPIs or automatic partial rollback to previous routing policy

Gate matrix (manual gates during launch window):
- Gate A: Canary health (first 24h) -> Criteria: errors < 0.5%, p95 < 350ms -> Action: proceed to Phase 2 or hold
- Gate B: Autoscaling stability -> Criteria: no oscillation > 3x scale events per hour -> Action: revert scaler policy and hold rollout
- Gate C: Customer feedback triage -> Criteria: no P1 CS tickets from pilot cohort -> Action: proceed; otherwise run remediation cadence

Primary contingency playbook (ordered, concise):
1) Severity: Critical customer impact (>=1% errors or data availability issue)
   - Immediate: Set system to conservative routing (route to stable model variant), disable new canary traffic via rollout console (owner: Maya Patel).
   - Pager: eng-sre on-call, platform-eng, product-ops.
   - Follow-up: Kickoff incident bridge (#incident-launch), runroot cause triage, decision within 30m to rollback or mitigate.

2) Severity: Latency explosion (p95 > 450ms sustained 3m)
   - Immediate: Throttle non-critical features (batching disabled endpoints), increase instance concurrency cap where safe (SRE action), and pause further rollouts.
   - If throttling doesn't restore SLO in 10m: rollback rollout to previous routing policy and scale up Dedicated capacity (if reserved pools available).

3) Severity: Cost anomaly (cost > baseline +30% sustained 1h)
   - Immediate: Notify finance and product-ops. Evaluate rollback to quantized model variants or reduce non-critical caching TTLs.
   - If cost continues: temporary cap on per-customer token throughput for new customers (CS-managed).

Rollback quick steps (checked and rehearsed):
- Disable canary in Console -> revert traffic allocation to previous route (Console path: Product > Rollouts > Active).
- Re-pin model version on Dedicated pools (use dedicated route fallback).
- Notify customers on status page and send targeted message via CS playbook.

CS & external comms templates (short):
- Status page: "We are investigating an issue affecting latency for a subset of requests. We have rolled back a recent routing change and are monitoring. No data loss. More updates in 30m."
- Pilot cohort message: "Thanks for the report — we've reverted today's change and will follow up with a timeline for re-testing. Apologies for the disruption; your feedback is prioritized."

Post-launch debrief template (to fill within 48h):
- Executive summary (1-2 sentences)
- What happened (timeline)
- Impact (numbers: error %, affected customers, duration)
- Root cause (hypothesis + confirmed)
- Actions taken (rollback, config change)
- Follow-ups (owners + due dates)
- Lessons learned & runbook updates

Risk register (short form):
- Risk: Autoscaler oscillation on model cache warm-up | Mitigation: cap cold-start concurrency, pre-warm caches | Owner: Jordan Lee
- Risk: Regressions from quantization variant | Mitigation: narrower eval set, pre-rollout A/B comparison | Owner: Camila Ruiz
- Risk: CS burden during phase increases | Mitigation: CS playbook + dedicated triage channel + scripted templates | Owner: Maya Patel

Unresolved questions / To do (notes to self):
- Confirm backup Dedicated GPUS pool size available for emergency scale (ask infra on-call).
- Validate that billing anomaly alert is fired within 5m (Ben to confirm).
- Add a short playbook for 'partial model fallback' to services/runbooks - small cheat sheet for on-call.

Links & quick refs:
- Canary cohort list (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-12345
- PR for autoscaler changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ramp-pr/342
- Incident guideline template: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE
- Slack channel for launch: #prodops-launch

Notes: this doc is intentionally concise and meant to be a single source of truth during the 2-week rollout. Keep it lightweight: if a decision requires a larger postmortem, create a separate incident doc but link back here.
